messages.content: I need to open a separate trip for my spouse and me for a family wedding near Carlsbad in November. The rehearsal dinner is Friday evening, the wedding is Saturday afternoon, and we want Sunday by the coast before flying home Monday. We'd leave Denver Thursday and share one room for four nights.
What are the exact dates, and where are the two family events? The venue locations will determine whether staying in Carlsbad Village or farther south along the coast is more practical.

Thursday, November 6 through Monday, November 10. The rehearsal dinner is at a restaurant in Carlsbad Village at 6:30 Friday. The wedding is at Leo Carrillo Ranch, with guests asked to arrive by 3:00 Saturday.

That makes Carlsbad Village the stronger hotel base for Friday and for a walkable Sunday, while Leo Carrillo Ranch is roughly a 15- to 25-minute drive depending on traffic. For flights, should I keep the search to San Diego, and do you want a rental car or would you consider rideshares?
Use San Diego. Compare both ways. We won't need a car for most of Sunday, so I don't want to assume renting one is automatically better.

Understood. A Thursday Denver departure around late morning or early afternoon would put you at SAN before the evening commute becomes difficult. On Monday, would you rather preserve part of the morning in Carlsbad or get back to Denver earlier?
Preserve the morning, but I don't want a very late arrival home. Aim for a nonstop leaving San Diego between noon and 3:00.

There are generally nonstop choices on that route from United, Southwest, and sometimes Frontier, but the exact November schedule and fares need a live check. A useful working pair is Thursday departing DEN around 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., arriving SAN around 12:30 to 2:30 p.m., and Monday departing SAN around 12:30 to 2:30 p.m., reaching Denver in the late afternoon. For the hotel, is being directly across from or beside the beach enough, or do you need an ocean-view room?
Walking distance is enough. A balcony or partial view would be pleasant, but don't let that push the room over $300 a night before tax.

Three bases merit comparison. Tamarack Beach Resort is across from the beach and about a 10- to 15-minute walk to central Carlsbad Village. Beach Terrace is directly above the beach and closer to the Village, but rooms can exceed the cap. Cape Rey is across from South Carlsbad State Beach and has a resort setting, though it is several miles from the rehearsal dinner and the walkable village area. I would price Tamarack first, Beach Terrace only if a qualifying room appears, and Cape Rey as the southern alternative.
Build actual trip combinations around those. Include airport transport, Friday dinner, Saturday wedding, and what Sunday would realistically look like.

Combination A: a midday Thursday nonstop to SAN, a rental car collected at the airport, and four nights at Tamarack. Drive about 40 to 55 minutes to Carlsbad outside peak congestion, park at the hotel, and walk to Friday's dinner. On Saturday, allow 30 minutes for the drive to Leo Carrillo Ranch plus parking and arrive by 2:40. Leave the car parked Sunday and walk the seawall, beach, Village shops, and restaurants. Monday, check out around 10:30, drive to SAN, return the car, and target a 1:00 to 2:00 p.m. nonstop. This is the most balanced arrangement.
What would that cost, roughly, for both of us? Separate firm figures from estimates.

Nothing is firm without a live search. Planning estimates for two travelers are $500 to $850 total for nonstop economy airfare, $900 to $1,200 before hotel tax for four nights at Tamarack, and $260 to $380 for a five-day rental after ordinary taxes but before fuel, parking, or optional coverage. That puts the core trip near $1,660 to $2,430, plus hotel taxes, meals, fuel, and any hotel parking charge. The airfare and room rate are the largest variables.
Now do Beach Terrace without a rental car. I want to see whether paying more for the room could still work overall.

Combination B: use the same flight windows, take a rideshare from SAN to Beach Terrace on Thursday, and remain car-free. Walk to the rehearsal dinner Friday. For Saturday, schedule a rideshare to Leo Carrillo Ranch around 2:05, leaving extra time because pickup availability near the venue after the reception may be uneven; arranging a local car service for the return would be safer than relying on an immediate app pickup. Sunday is fully walkable: beach access, the seawall, Carlsbad Village, and dinner without transport. Monday, leave the hotel about three hours before the flight for the rideshare to SAN.
Price that one, and account for the Saturday return problem rather than hiding it.

Use $500 to $850 for flights, about $1,000 to $1,400 before tax for four nights if Beach Terrace has a room near your ceiling, $90 to $140 for the two airport rides, $35 to $55 outbound to the ranch, and approximately $80 to $150 for a prearranged Saturday return car. The working total is $1,705 to $2,595 before hotel tax and meals. It can approach the rental-car plan at the low end, but only if the room stays close to $300 and the event return is reserved in advance.
And Cape Rey? It looks attractive, but I suspect it complicates the weekend.

Combination C: pair Cape Rey with a rental car. It is convenient to the coast and gives Sunday a quieter South Carlsbad focus: walk along the bluff and beach near Ponto, use the resort, then drive into the Village only if desired. Friday requires a roughly 10- to 20-minute drive to the Village, so one of you would need to avoid alcohol or use rideshares. Saturday's drive to Leo Carrillo Ranch is generally practical, around 15 to 25 minutes. Monday's drive to SAN is shorter than from the Village, though traffic can still expand it.
Could Cape Rey work without the car if we use rideshares for both family events?

It could, but it is the weakest car-free combination. You would add rides both ways Friday, both ways Saturday, and to and from SAN, while losing the ability to walk into the Village. A realistic transport allowance is about $260 to $430, with the same concern about late pickup from the ranch. Unless Cape Rey is materially cheaper than Tamarack or you specifically want its resort facilities, the added logistics do not buy much.
Then narrow this to the two sensible choices. Also compare Monday timing. I don't want a nominal coastal morning that is really just packing and waiting for a car.

Keep A, Tamarack plus rental car, and B, Beach Terrace plus rides and a reserved Saturday car. With a 1:30 p.m. Monday flight, A should leave Carlsbad around 9:45 to allow for traffic, fuel, rental return, and security; that gives time only for breakfast and a short beach walk. B can usually leave around 10:00, depending on the rideshare estimate, and avoids rental return, but the difference is modest. A remains easier for Thursday arrival and the ranch; B is better only if the room rate is competitive and you value staying directly on the beach.
Give me complete working itineraries for A and B, including the decision points we still need to verify. Don't book either.

Option A: Thursday, November 6, take a DEN-SAN nonstop departing roughly 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.; collect a rental car and reach Tamarack Beach Resort in the afternoon. Stay four nights in one room. Friday is open until walking to the 6:30 p.m. rehearsal dinner in Carlsbad Village. Saturday, leave the hotel around 2:05 p.m. for Leo Carrillo Ranch and plan to be parked by 2:40. Sunday, keep the car parked and spend the day on the beach, seawall, and in the Village. Monday, have breakfast and a short coastal walk, leave about 9:45 for SAN, return the car, and take a nonstop between 12:30 and 2:30 p.m.

Option B: use the same flight targets and stay four nights at Beach Terrace. Take rideshares between SAN and the hotel, walk to Friday dinner, and leave by prebooked car around 2:05 Saturday. Reserve the post-reception return with a named pickup location and flexible pickup window. Spend Sunday entirely on foot at the beach and in the Village. Leave around 10:00 Monday for the same return-flight window.

Before choosing, verify live nonstop schedules and total airfare for two, baggage and seat terms, each hotel's exact room category and all-in four-night price, parking and resort fees, cancellation deadlines, and whether a balcony or view is guaranteed or merely requested. For A, compare the rental's all-in price, coverage, fuel terms, and hotel parking. For B, obtain a written Saturday car-service quote and confirm after-hours pickup at Leo Carrillo Ranch. Also check the wedding invitation for parking or shuttle instructions and recalculate every drive against current traffic estimates. Nothing has been booked.
